title: Every button, link and field has a name
note: Every visible button, link and field has a name a screen reader can say: text, aria-label or a label element.
intent: An icon-only button is a button with no name: a screen reader says "button" and a person using voice control cannot ask for it. Give every control its name where a person would look for it: visible text for buttons and links, a <label for> (or a wrapping <label>) for every field, and aria-label only where the design truly has no room for text (an icon button gets aria-label="Delete task" and a title). A placeholder is not a label: it disappears when you type. Names should say what the control does in this context ("Delete task: Buy milk"), not repeat "button" or "click here". The page reports how many displayed controls it could not name in state().ui.unnamedControls and which ones in ui.unnamedSample.

check.note: Every displayed button, link and field has an accessible name; the page counts the ones that do not in state().ui.unnamedControls.

port: Whoever writes a component writes its label with it: icon buttons take a required `label` argument, fields are built by one helper that always emits the <label>.
